chunks: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about a man who is killed during the Sacred Month — what is his diyah? He said: 'A diyah and one-third.'

key_terms.الشَّهْر الْحَرَام: al-Shahr al-Haram — the Sacred Month, one of the four months in the Islamic lunar calendar (Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah) during which warfare and killing are specially prohibited
key_terms.ثُلُث: thulutha — one-third; the additional increment added to the base diyah for killing during a Sacred Month
key_terms.دِيَة: diyah — the monetary compensation paid to the victim's family as blood money for homicide or bodily harm, a foundational concept in Islamic criminal jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a person killed during the Sacred Month according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the enhanced blood money (diyah) owed for a person killed during one of the four Sacred Months (Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab). The ruling establishes that the diyah increases by one-third as a consequence of the sanctity of these months, which were already observed in pre-Islamic Arabia and then reaffirmed in Islam. This increase reflects the gravity of violating the sacred prohibition on bloodshed during these months, a ruling that jurists classify under the enhancement of penalties for crimes committed in sacred times and places.
